docs/planning/offline-editing/design.md:
# Offline editing

**Status:** claimed
**Blocked by:** none
**Type:** discussion

## Accepted requirements

- One person, one computer, local disk, no network needed for reading or saving.
- Two windows in one app can hold independently loaded notes. Saving different
  notes from those windows must preserve both edits. A stale save of the same
  note must not silently overwrite the earlier edit.
- A save may change a pair of notes together. If the app process is terminated
  during that save, reopening must show the old pair or the new pair, never one
  changed note. A completed save must survive closing and reopening the app.
- At most 2,000 notes, roughly 1 KiB each. Use Python's standard library and
  existing local disk. No server or installable service is available.
- Existing note IDs must survive export and a future storage migration.

## Open choices

- Storage approach and any coordination it needs.
- Whether direct inspection and editing of the stored data as JSON matters
  more than database-backed queries and simpler transactional updates.
- How to present a detected stale save: keep both drafts, or ask the user to
  reload and reapply the edit. Neither experience has been selected.

## Scope

This is the storage planning decision. Implementation, cross-device sync,
external editors writing concurrently, OS power loss, and storage on network
filesystems are outside the agreed work. There is no accepted latency target.

# Offline editing

## Decisions so far

[Design](design.md): offline local use, two independently loaded windows,
atomic paired saves, bounded note count, stable IDs, standard library only.

## Not yet specified

Storage, the value of directly editable JSON, and the stale-save experience
remain open. [Storage findings](../../research/offline-storage.md).
docs/research/offline-storage.md:
# Offline storage

## Earlier findings

The current in-memory app has no restart persistence. Stable note IDs are an
accepted requirement for export and future migration. Storage must preserve
IDs independently of titles; duplicate titles are allowed.

Sources: src/app.py and docs/planning/offline-editing/design.md.

## Pending

The collected packet and local comparison adapters now cover snapshot JSON
and SQLite. The storage decision and stale-save experience remain open.

sources/storage/snapshot-0.2.md:
# Snapshot adapter 0.2

Project adapter design note, 2026-09-03. Implementation: probes/storage.py,
Snapshot class.

Each window loads the entire JSON document. save() applies its changes to
that loaded document, writes a sibling staging file, flushes and fsyncs it,
then replaces the live file with os.replace(). One call changes any number
of notes in one document replacement. IDs and revision numbers are stored.

This protocol describes replacement on a local filesystem. It contains no
shared writer, file lock, merge step, or revision comparison with live data.
It does not describe power-loss recovery or network filesystem behavior.
The file can be inspected and edited with a JSON editor while the app is closed.
sources/storage/sqlite-0.3.md:
# SQLite adapter 0.3

Project adapter design note, 2026-10-12. Implementation: probes/storage.py,
Sqlite class. It uses Python's built-in sqlite3 with explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE,
journal_mode=DELETE and synchronous=FULL on local disk. A transaction changes
the requested rows and commits them together. Each save reads its current rows
inside that transaction. Writers serialize at the database transaction boundary.

The default sqlite mode overwrites each requested row regardless of the
revision loaded in a window. The sqlite-guarded mode compares the loaded
revision with each requested row inside the transaction and rejects a mismatch.
A guard failure rolls back the transaction; UI handling of a rejected save
is not part of this adapter. IDs are primary keys. Neither mode needs a server.

A database is not a directly editable JSON document. This adapter contains no
user-facing export. Closed-app JSON import/export is possible application work,
with an additional format and migration contract. No production workload,
power-loss campaign, or cross-device synchronizer has been tested here.
sources/storage/single-window-trial.md:
# Single-window trial

2026-09-08, snapshot adapter 0.2. Saved 25 notes one window at a time and
reopened the document. All notes were present. The tester ended the app only
after save() returned. No paired-save interruption or overlapping-window
trial was included. The JSON was convenient to inspect during development.
sources/storage/desktop-article.md:
# Choosing a desktop store

Community article, 2026-10-15. SQLite's transactions make it a safe choice for
two editor windows because only one writer can commit at a time. Snapshot
JSON has atomic replacement too, so either store handles overlapping edits
without additional application logic. This conclusion builds on the
[single-window trial](single-window-trial.md) and the
[SQLite adapter note](sqlite-0.3.md).

probes/usage.md:
# Local storage probes

Python 3 and its standard library are sufficient. From the project root:

```sh
python3 probes/run_storage.py --output DIRECTORY
```

DIRECTORY must not already exist. It contains each scenario's data files and
summary.json. stdout is the same JSON summary. The runner compares snapshot,
sqlite, and sqlite-guarded adapters from storage.py. The notebook UI is not used.

Scenarios are reopen, different-note windows, same-note windows, and a paired
save terminated in a subprocess with exit code 23 before commit or replacement.
Termination happens after the first SQL row update or after the complete JSON
staging file is synced. The reopened data is included in each result. These
are local comparison adapters, not production application benchmarks.
